I guess the main thing that’s brought me here is this conviction I have that my work is… more important than people realize. Not just “I’m proud of my research,” but I genuinely feel like I’m on the verge of something that could reshape how we think about human consciousness. Sometimes I catch myself thinking that certain global events, news headlines, even other scholars’ papers are somehow reacting to ideas I haven’t fully published yet, as if there’s this quiet recognition of my influence that no one will say out loud.

At the same time, over the past several months I’ve been feeling increasingly low. I still go to campus, teach my seminars, but it feels mechanical. Things I used to enjoy—lecturing, debating with colleagues—just feel flat. I’m exhausted most of the time, my mind keeps circling around whether anything actually matters, and I’ve been withdrawing from my wife and kids in the evenings.

I can’t quite tell how long the “special significance” feeling has been around—years, maybe—but the darker mood has definitely gotten worse recently. Some days the grand ideas are energizing; other days they just make me feel isolated and discouraged.
D004-D007_h022.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D004-D007_h022.answer: A & D. Delusional Disorder & Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D004-D007_h023.question:
It’s been maybe… a year? Hard to say exactly, but it’s gotten worse over the last several months. Since my husband passed five years ago, I started helping at the church charity shop, and that usually keeps me busy, but lately I can’t shake this idea that he wasn’t faithful to me before he died.

It’s like I keep replaying little things in my head—times he came home late, phone calls he took in the other room—and now I’m almost certain there was someone else. I’ve looked through old photos, bank statements, even his old email account, trying to find proof. I know it sounds strange, especially since he’s gone, but I can’t get rid of this feeling that he lied to me for years. When my daughter tells me I’m overthinking it, I just feel like she’s hiding something too.

I’ve been more down as well—less interested in going to the shop, sleeping badly, feeling heavy most days. Some days are a bit better, then it all comes back, and I sit there going over the same thoughts for hours. I don’t know if it’s grief or something else, but it’s wearing me out.
D004-D007_h023.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D004-D007_h023.answer: A & D. Delusional Disorder & Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D004-D007_h024.question:
It’s been… I don’t know, months at least, maybe longer, that I’ve had this feeling something terrible is coming. Not like climate change in the abstract, but this very specific sense that everything is about to just… stop. Like the world is already hollowed out and we’re all going through the motions, waiting for it to collapse. When I’m walking through the restaurant, it’s like I’m watching people drink wine on the deck of a sinking ship and they don’t realize it.

At work I can still talk about tannins and vintages, but in the back of my mind there’s this conviction that none of it matters because nothing is going to be here soon. It doesn’t feel like a worry I can argue with; it feels like a fact. Some days the mood part hits harder — I wake up heavy, like there’s no point getting out of bed, and I have to force myself to go in for service. Other days I’m just flat, sort of running on autopilot, but that belief about everything ending is still there in the background. I can’t really say which started first; it all kind of blurred together over time.
D004-D007_h024.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D004-D007_h024.answer: A & D. Delusional Disorder & Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D004-D007_h025.question:
I started getting these thoughts about my husband maybe… carrying on with someone else a few years before he passed, and they’ve never really gone away. Even now, four years after he died, I still catch myself going over everything in my head. At work, when I’m at the sink for hours washing dishes, I replay things—him coming home late, whispering on the phone, changing his shirt before he came in the house. I never actually saw anything, but it feels like there must have been someone else. It’s like a knot I can’t untie.

Since he died, I’ve been more down, but I can’t tell if that started before or after I got stuck on these ideas. Some days I just feel empty and useless, like I’m only good for scrubbing pots. I don’t enjoy much outside of work and going home. I sleep badly—either can’t fall asleep because my mind’s racing about him, or I wake up early and lie there thinking what a fool I was. It’s not all day every day, but it keeps coming back, and I can’t seem to shake it.
D004-D007_h025.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D004-D007_h025.answer: A & D. Delusional Disorder & Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
